svg.title: The two routes by which processing becomes lawful under the DPDP Act. The consent route runs in five steps: a notice served before the request, a clear affirmative action by the individual, a record the fiduciary keeps because the burden of proof is its own, withdrawal made as easy as giving, and stopping and erasing once consent is withdrawn. The legitimate-uses route is a closed list covering data the individual volunteered for that purpose, employment purposes, medical emergencies and public health, and legal obligations to the State. There is no legitimate-interests ground and no contract-performance ground, so anything outside the list needs consent.
svg.text: TWO WAYS PROCESSING BECOMES LAWFUL — AND ONLY TWO

g.text: Route A — Consent
the default for anything commercial
Notice, served before you ask
What data, what purpose, how to withdraw, how to complain
— in English or any Eighth Schedule language, at their choice
A clear affirmative action
An unticked box the person ticks. Not a pre-tick,
not scrolling, not continued use of the site.
A record you can produce later
Which notice version, which purposes, when, by what action.
The burden of proving it is yours, not theirs.
Withdrawal, as easy as giving
If consent took one tap, withdrawal cannot take an email
to support and a five-day wait.
Then stop, and erase
You stop, your processors stop, and the data goes — unless
some other law requires you to keep it.
Route B — Legitimate uses
a closed list, not a catch-all
Data they volunteered for that very purpose,
having not said no to it
Employment, and protecting the employer
from loss or liability
Medical emergency, epidemic, disaster,
breakdown of public order
Court orders, disclosures the law compels,
State subsidies and benefits
Not on the list, and people assume they are:
“We have a legitimate interest in it”
“It is necessary to perform the contract”
“They were already our customer”

svg.text: Anything outside Route B needs Route A. And if you cannot produce the notice and the consent record, you are treated as never having had consent.
